analysis:
I examined the Gemma4 changes, which add tensor-parallel (TP) as a supported generation mode alongside the pipeline. The reviewed files are Gemma4PlacementFamily.swift, Gemma4StageGeometry.swift, Gemma4ResidentAdapterDefinition.swift, Gemma4StateBudget.swift, the new Gemma4TensorParallelRequestBudget.swift, and the patch excerpt of Gemma4RequestGeometry.swift. I found no concrete security regression.

Geometry validation is unchanged. Gemma4StageGeometry.swift only extracts the constants routedExperts=128 and expertsPerToken=8 and still compares them against the configuration.

The budget logic reduces to metadata arithmetic. Gemma4StateBudget.estimate keeps the default ranks=1, so pipeline results and the pinned 719,380,600-byte check should be unchanged. Ranks are restricted to {1,2} with divisibility guards. The new Gemma4TensorParallelRequestBudget uses the checked product and sum helpers and validates the allocator bound (allocated >= logical). Overflow and underflow paths appear to throw instead of wrapping.

The prefix cache posture is unchanged in kind. Gemma4ResidentAdapterDefinition.swift line 18 sets tensorParallelKeepsPromptPrefixes=true and says TP keeps prompt prefixes resident and on the owner's SSD tier. This relates to T-041 (the cross-tenant prefix-cache oracle, SEC-035) and to A-001. I could not confirm that Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix scopes entries by cacheSalt, uses HMAC-keyed tags, or applies the TTL. The new TP prefix capture code and the TP resident runtime are not in the supplied evidence.

TP is a new collective path between two cluster ranks, using sealed frames (QwenTensorParallelSealCodec). Its authentication, peer trust and consumer-data exposure sit outside the supplied files.

The budget notes that the activation floor is a conservative constant, not a measured value. The prefix memory tier is also not charged and is said to give way under pressure. This is a memory availability assumption rather than a verified control.

I could not review the Gemma4RequestGeometry.swift hunk fully, because only a patch excerpt was supplied for it. The visible hunk checks kinds against the plan layer by layer.

Next-pass questions are whether Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix keeps the salt scoping and HMAC naming that T-041 requires, and whether the TP resident runtime and load agreement keep the TB-007 and T-041 mitigations. I am setting needs_deeper_review because these unsupplied components affect the security conclusion.
